examples.name: creation-and-indexing
examples.summary: Create arrays and read elements/rows. Runs on both backends.

examples.name: slicing-strides
examples.summary: Strided and negative slicing (NumPy's start:stop:step on a 1-D array). Runs on both backends.

examples.name: connected-components
examples.summary: Connected components of a graph from its adjacency matrix.

examples.name: dominant-frequency
examples.summary: Find the dominant frequency of a sampled signal with the real FFT. Both backends.
examples.equivalent: NumPy: F = np.fft.rfft(x); freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(n, d=1/fs); freqs[np.argmax(np.abs(F))]

examples.name: roundtrip
examples.summary: The inverse FFT undoes the forward FFT. Both backends.

examples.name: npy-roundtrip
examples.summary: Save and load arrays in NumPy's .npy and .npz formats (interchangeable with NumPy).

examples.name: validation-rule
examples.summary: Validate an incoming numeric array by shape and finiteness with the Laravel rule.

examples.name: solve-and-fit
examples.summary: Dense linear algebra: solve a square system, and least-squares fit an overdetermined one.
examples.equivalent: NumPy: np.linalg.solve(A, b); np.linalg.lstsq(A, y, rcond=None)

examples.name: out-parameter
examples.summary: Write ufunc results into a preallocated array with the out= parameter (no new allocation).
examples.equivalent: NumPy: np.sqrt(x, out=buf); np.multiply(x, 2, out=x)  (in place)

examples.name: ufuncs
examples.summary: Element-wise math (ufuncs), scalar and array broadcasting. Runs on both backends.
examples.equivalent: NumPy: a + 1; np.sqrt(x); a.prod(); np.add(mat, col) broadcasting (3,) over (2, 3)

examples.name: value-iteration
examples.summary: Solve a small Markov decision process with value iteration.

examples.name: bounded-lbfgsb
examples.summary: Box-constrained minimisation. Passing `bounds` switches minimize to L-BFGS-B automatically.
examples.equivalent: SciPy: scipy.optimize.minimize(f, x0, method='L-BFGS-B', bounds=[(-2, 0.5), (None, None)])

examples.name: breakeven-brentq
examples.summary: Bracketed root finding with Brent's method.

examples.name: decay-leastsq
examples.summary: Nonlinear least squares from an explicit residual function (Levenberg-Marquardt).

examples.name: demand-curve-fit
examples.summary: Nonlinear curve fitting.
examples.equivalent: SciPy: scipy.optimize.curve_fit(model, xdata, ydata, p0)  ->  (params, covariance)

examples.name: implied-yield-newton
examples.summary: Newton's method for a scalar root (no bracket needed, uses a numerical derivative here).

examples.name: nelder-mead-fmin
examples.summary: Derivative-free minimisation with the Nelder-Mead simplex via fmin.

examples.name: rosenbrock-bfgs
examples.summary: Unconstrained minimisation with quasi-Newton BFGS.

examples.name: monte-carlo
examples.summary: A seeded Monte-Carlo simulation, vectorised. Runs on both backends.

examples.name: numpy-seed
examples.summary: Reproduce a NumPy random stream from a seed, and snapshot/restore generator state.

examples.name: dataset-statistics
examples.summary: Reductions along axes: per-column and per-row statistics of a small dataset. Both backends.
examples.equivalent: NumPy: a.sum(); a.mean(axis=0); a.std(axis=0, ddof=1); a.max(axis=1)

examples.name: leaderboard
examples.summary: Sort, rank, and binary-search a 1-D array. Both backends.
examples.equivalent: NumPy: np.sort(a) == a.sort-copy; a.argsort(); np.searchsorted(sorted, v)

examples.name: conjugate-gradient
examples.summary: Solve a sparse symmetric positive-definite system with conjugate gradient.
examples.equivalent: SciPy: scipy.sparse.linalg.cg(A, b)  ->  (x, info)   (info == 0 means converged)

examples.name: combinatorics
examples.summary: Combinatorics with the gamma family. Both backends.

examples.name: logistic-and-erf
examples.summary: Two workhorse special functions: the logistic sigmoid and the error function. Both backends.

examples.name: ab-test
examples.summary: A/B test: a two-sample t-test on a per-user metric. Both backends.

examples.name: linear-regression
examples.summary: Ordinary least-squares line fit with correlation and significance. Both backends.
examples.equivalent: SciPy: scipy.stats.linregress(x, y)  ->  slope, intercept, rvalue, pvalue, stderr, ...

examples.name: normal-distribution
examples.summary: Work with a distribution object: pdf/cdf/ppf of the standard normal. Both backends.
